clue.text: Unlit ground, with footballer initially locked inside

parts.note: a pitch is a playing ground, as for football or cricket

indicators.note: inside says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a back is a defensive footballer, such as a full-back

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A footballer is locked in a dark, unlit stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes L from 'locked', and 'inside' puts that L into BACK to give BLACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere pitch-black has no light at all, so it is completely unlit.

clue.text: Advertise pastry dessert

definitions.meaning: to ... a product is to promote it with exaggerated praise
a cream ... is a light choux pastry dessert

explanation.definitionFit: Puff is both overblown promotion as a verb and a light hollow pastry, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Raising loan, bachelor leaves promises to pay for flat

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means turning the letters upwards, read backwards
leaves means goes away from, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a loan creates a debt for the borrower
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: Someone borrows, and with the bachelor gone, writes IOUs to cover a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' drops B from DEBT leaving DET, which 'Raising' turns upwards in this down clue to TED. 'Flat' looks like a home but means dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat in the sense of dull and lifeless is a synonym of wearisome and boring.

clue.text: Reach Londoner's unusual back door

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters are arranged in an uncommon new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A Londoner reaches an odd rear entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the thirteen letters of REACH and LONDONER (the possessive adds none). 'back door' is used as an adjective meaning underhand.
explanation.definitionFit: Back-door as an adjective means secret and underhand, just as hole-and-corner dealings are furtive.

clue.text: Pretentious boy and girl

parts.note: a lad is a boy
Ida is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A snooty young couple, a boy and a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da is an informal word for affected, snobbish and pretentious manners.

clue.text: Whale providing ready money, it's said —- and plenty of it!

indicators.note: it's said marks a word spoken aloud that is written differently

parts.note: cash is ready money, notes and coins
a lot means plenty

explanation.surface: A whale that brings in money, and lots of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' gives the sound of CASH, spelt CACH to begin the whale's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The cachalot is another name for the sperm whale.

clue.text: — Bother!

definitions.meaning: the printed punctuation mark is itself one sense: the line called by this name
an exclamation of annoyance, a mild oath like drat

explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation stroke is named a dash, and Dash! is a dated mild curse of irritation.

clue.text: New arrangement bringing together a pair of animals

parts.note: a nag is a horse, one of the pair of animals
a ram is a male sheep, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: A new arrangement brings two animals together.
explanation.definitionFit: A word made by rearranging letters is literally a new arrangement of them.

clue.text: Artist's first name is hard, a mixture of yours and mine

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: a mixture of says the letters of the words that follow are blended together

explanation.surface: A painter's forename is said to be hard, a blend of yours and mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a mixture of' rearranges YOURS and MINE into IERONYMUS. The artist is Hieronymus Bosch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch painter Bosch was named Hieronymus, so it is his first name.

clue.text: Female didn't hurry, bearing daughter, and wasted time

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: to idle is to take one's time and not hurry

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman took her time, then had a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' has IDLED carry D inside it, making IDDLED after F.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle about is to waste time on trivial things.

clue.text: Turn up with several notes on military decoration

parts.note: to cock is to tilt or turn up, as a hat brim or ear
A, D and E are musical notes

explanation.surface: A soldier turns up with a few notes about a decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockade is a rosette or knot of ribbon worn on a hat as a military badge.

clue.text: University in contact with local exchange to demand explanation

indicators.note: exchange means the letters swap places to form something new

explanation.surface: A university links up with the local telephone exchange to ask for an explanation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange' looks like part of a telephone exchange but rearranges U, CONTACT and LOCAL together.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone to account is to demand that they justify or explain their conduct.

clue.text: Scamp washing baby has to prepare vegetables

definitions.meaning: to wash only an infant's face and bottom, a quick perfunctory clean
to trim both ends off beans or gooseberries before cooking

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means removing both ends of produce, and also washing just the face and bottom of an infant.

clue.text: Letter rejecting zero hour

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A letter turning down a zero-hour arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns OHR backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rho is the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Where circuits may be tried out, and doorsteps produced

definitions.text: Where circuits may be tried out
definitions.meaning: a board on which electronic circuits are prototyped without soldering
a board on which thick slices of loaf, informally doorsteps, are cut

explanation.walkthrough: A doorstep is British slang for a very thick slice of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronics prototypers use one to test circuits, and in the kitchen it is where thick slices are cut.

clue.text: Occupy chair, but not quietly

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to chair a meeting is to preside over it
P stands for piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: Take the chair, but keep quiet about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes P from PRESIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To occupy a house is to live in it, to dwell there.

clue.text: Securing trip by ship, or possibly, given extra time, by motor

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Arranging a voyage by ship, or perhaps, with more time, by car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given extra' adds T to BY MOTOR, and 'possibly' rearranges the lot. Bottomry is a loan secured on a ship to finance a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottomry was a maritime contract pledging the vessel itself as security for money to fund a voyage.

clue.text: Bugs police chief caught in the act? On the contrary

indicators.note: caught in would put one piece inside another
On the contrary says the stated containment is reversed, so the act goes inside the chief

parts.note: Lavrentiy Beria was head of Stalin's secret police

explanation.surface: A police chief is caught red-handed planting bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught in' alone would wrap the chief inside the act; 'On the contrary' flips that, so the act goes inside. Beria ran Stalin's secret police.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs is an everyday word for germs, and bacteria are such microbes.

clue.text: In 30 days parking alongside cricket ground will get green light

indicators.note: In places the first piece inside the next

parts.note: April, abbreviated APR, is a month of thirty days
the Oval is a London cricket ground

explanation.surface: Parking beside a cricket ground gets the go-ahead within a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts P inside APR, giving APPR. The Oval is a Test cricket ground in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: The green light is idiomatic for permission to proceed, an official go-ahead.

clue.text: Combustibles mostly in the middle of monument

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a pyre is a heap of combustible material for burning a body
amid means in the middle of

explanation.surface: Fuel stacked inside a great monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts PYRE to PYR.
explanation.definitionFit: The pyramids of Egypt are among the most famous monuments ever built.

clue.text: New driver with gold carriage

parts.note: L is the learner plate for a new driver
and means with, together
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A learner driver takes a gold carriage out.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding top.

clue.text: Doctor, medic's hiding drug inside drink

indicators.note: hiding means concealing, so one piece holds the other
inside confirms the drug goes within the medic

parts.note: DR is a medic, with the possessive S
E is the slang abbreviation for ecstasy
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A doctor spikes a drink with a hidden drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' and 'inside' both signal the drug going within the medic, giving DRES. Doctor here means disguise or falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor something is to falsify or embellish it, much as one might dress it up.

clue.text: Can petrel set about skua's head?

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a prion is a small petrel of southern oceans

indicators.note: head asks for the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Can a seabird attack a skua's head?
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes S from 'skua's', and 'set about' places PRION around it. Can is slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The can is American slang for jail, a place of confinement.

clue.text: Save some superb architecture

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters lie within the words

explanation.surface: Preserve a piece of fine architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: Save here means except, as in 'all save one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bar and save both mean except, as in 'everyone bar him'.

clue.text: Unsporting sandpiper heard by insect

indicators.note: heard marks a word spoken aloud that is spelt differently

parts.note: the knot is a wading bird of the sandpiper family
a cricket is a chirping insect

explanation.surface: A wading bird ignores the rules, overheard by an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not cricket' is a British idiom for unfair, from the gentlemanly bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes behaviour that is unfair or against the spirit of fair play.

clue.text: Sort letters

definitions.meaning: a kind or category, as in 'that sort of thing'
printed characters, as set by a printer

explanation.definitionFit: Type means a kind, and also the printed characters on a page.

clue.text: Suitor when married changes

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the word next to it shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A suitor's attitude shifts once he is wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges MARRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor courts someone, so he is an admirer.

clue.text: Yielding game to unknown

parts.note: squash is a racket game
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Giving up a game to a stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: Squashy means soft and easily pressed, giving way under pressure.

clue.text: Queen killed herself — oh, I say!

parts.note: did herself in, killed herself, shortened to did
O is a spelling of the exclamation oh

explanation.surface: An exclamation at the news that a queen took her own life.
explanation.walkthrough: Dido, Queen of Carthage, killed herself when Aeneas left; 'I say!' is surface exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido was the legendary founder and Queen of Carthage in Virgil's Aeneid.

clue.text: Agricultural building an important element in Devon location

parts.note: a barn is a farm building
a staple is a main or important element

explanation.surface: A farm building is a key feature of a place in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnstaple is a market town in north Devon, in England.
